title: Ex 2.5 #5 · Truth table for (P ∧ ∼P) ∨ Q
prompt: Build a truth table for $(P \wedge \sim P) \vee Q$ and enter the truth value of the whole statement in each row.
answer_format: Four T/F values, one per row, top to bottom, like T F T T. Rows (P, Q) go TT, TF, FT, FF, as in the book. Helper columns are optional steps, like ~P : F F T T.
hints: Look at P ∧ ∼P first. Can P and ∼P ever both be true?
Once you know the column of P ∧ ∼P, or-ing it with Q is quick.
solution: $P \wedge \sim P$ is false in every row, since $P$ and $\sim P$ always have opposite values.
So $(P \wedge \sim P) \vee Q$ has the same truth value as $Q$: T F T F.

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses the truth tables for ∧, ∨, ∼, ⇒ and ⇔ (Sections 2.2–2.5).
